name: std/system
description: The host a program runs on: files, the trap handler and its stack traces, the dynamic loader and the object file it reads, the command interpreter and the standard streams, and what a process can say about itself.
residual: Split out of std/runtime 2026-08-16. These are the modules that used to be called runtime and are not: every one of them imports the library (Traps -> Streams, Loader -> Files, Commands -> Modules + Streams), so they sit above std/base rather than below it.

Traps, Reflection and TrapWriters are one family and the trap handler is arguably runtime -- Go puts panic and the traceback in its runtime. Ours cannot: it prints through Streams. Left here rather than given a special case.

HostLibs, In and Out entered 2026-08-24, named by no package before and therefore not in the payload -- and that had consequences outside the tree: without HostLibs (dlopen by name, the foundation of every FFI binding) community/fftw, community/freeimage and community/usb do not compile at all, and without Out six modules that community/matrix ships do not either. In and Out are FOF's teaching console I/O over Commands + Streams, nothing more.

PrecisionTimer (Alexey Morozov, a Unix and a Windows implementation of one module) and Stopwatch over it entered 2026-08-24: a clock finer than Kernel's ticks is a host facility, and ocp's WMRaycaster is one of the things that could not be built without it.
FSTools entered 2026-08-24: file and directory commands over Files, host work, named by no package before.

The system-events and logging family entered 2026-08-24, unclaimed until then: Errors (system-wide error codes), EventsUtils with its three sinks (kernel log, memory, file), and FileTrapWriter. KernelLogger and MultiLogger are marked graphical -- both write through TextUtilities, which is std/gui's.

A dozen host-facing modules entered 2026-08-24, none of them claimed by any package before: what the machine is (CPUID, Info, UpTime, MemoryReader), what it does on its own (Autostart, BootConsole, TaskScheduler, Reboot), what it measures (HierarchicalProfiler and its aid), what it says about modules (DependencyWalker), localization, and the two binary-to-text converters.
ActiveTimers and ShellCommands entered 2026-08-24 because the check named them: the payload pulled them in through TVDriver and Telnet while no package claimed them.
FileHandlers (negelef) entered 2026-08-24: opening a file by what it is is host work.
PositionDebugging entered 2026-08-24, beside Traps and Reflection. All of these turned out to reach the window system (the check named them), so they are marked graphical and stay out of the payload.
